pete_acme: Hey team — noticing intermittent 504/timeouts on our batch embedding requests to /v1/embeddings. Billing also spiked this morning. Sample request IDs: req_abc123, req_def456. Happening ~2/5 batches. Can share logs.

maria_support: Sorry about that, Pete. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + python/js/go) that hits the same endpoint and a short sample of the server logs that include those request IDs? Also confirm model name and approximate batch size. If you can run with REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 that'll help. :pray:

pete_acme: Quick answers — model: text-embed-32k, batch_size: 128 (we batch embeddings for lists of docs). Minimal curl we used:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-32k","inputs":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_size":128}' \
  --max-time 30
```

python quick test we ran:

```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
json = {"model":"text-embed-32k","inputs": ["a"]*128}
r = requests.post(url, json=json, headers=headers, timeout=30)
print(r.status_code, r.text)
```

Logs tail with request id: 
`2026-03-01T10:12:34Z INFO request_id=req_abc123 start embedding batch_size=128`
`2026-03-01T10:12:64Z ERROR request_id=req_abc123 upstream_timeout after 30s`

maria_support: perfect — thanks. Ryan/SRE, can you take a look at infra traces? Ryan, any quick asks for Pete (extra headers, trace IDs)?

ryan_sre: Please ask Pete to capture the full request/response headers for a failed call and try a smaller batch_size (e.g., 16) to see if it reproduces. Also run the same curl but add `-H "X-Request-ID: <uuid>"` so we can map to infra traces. If you can, run `rdw-debug collect --request-ids req_abc123,req_def456` and attach the bundle.

sam_sdk: Also mention SDK version. If you're using our python SDK older than 0.9.4 we had a retry behavior that could amplify load. Quick python SDK repro (minimal):

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY", timeout=30, max_retries=2)
resp = client.embeddings.create(model="text-embed-32k", inputs=["a"]*128)
print(resp)
```

If you can try `max_retries=0` and smaller batch_size that'll tell us if retries are causing the spike.

alex_eng: FYI infra saw a brief fan-out to fallback workers around the same window. @ryan_sre I left a note in infra logs with infra-id infra-7789. Pete, can you also share the exact timestamps (UTC) when you saw the billing spike? That helps correlate cloud billing events vs retries.

pete_acme: timestamps: 2026-03-01T10:11:50Z -> 2026-03-01T10:15:00Z. I ran smaller batch (16) as requested — that completed. Re-ran original batch of 128 and it timed out. Added X-Request-ID: req_retry987 to header. Here are the new failing IDs: req_def456, req_retry987.

maria_support: great repro — thanks. Can you upload the app logs that include `req_def456` + `req_retry987` and attach the debug bundle from `rdw-debug`? If you can't run rdw-debug, paste an anonymized portion of the logs with timestamps. :lock:

pete_acme: uploaded bundle to shared link (private) and pasted a short snip here: 
`2026-03-01T10:13:02Z WARN request_id=req_def456 retrying after 500ms`
`2026-03-01T10:13:35Z ERROR request_id=req_def456 504 gateway_timeout`

ryan_sre: From infra side — likely we're hitting a KV cache pressure point when batch_size > 64 for that model on certain worker variants. Temporary mitigation: reduce batch_size or pin a lower memory variant. Long term we'll add a better backpressure signal. For now, Pete, can you switch to batch_size=64 and set SDK max_retries=1? That should avoid the retry storm.

sam_sdk: We're about to cut a minor SDK patch to add a configurable per-call max_concurrent_batches flag — ETA ~1h. I'll DM you when it's out, Pete. In the meantime try this JS snippet to set per-call timeout and no retries: 

```js
import Redwood from 'redwood';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, timeout: 30000, retries: 0 });
await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'text-embed-32k', inputs: new Array(64).fill('a') });
```

alex_eng: Also check if your app is accidentally parallelizing the same batch (double-submit). Logging X-Request-ID server-side will help ensure idempotency. If you want, add an idempotency token header `Idempotency-Key` to dedupe.

pete_acme: Follow-ups — ran with batch_size=64 + retries=1, all good for 20 runs. Billing looked normal. Thank you all. How can we automatically capture the X-Request-ID from the SDK responses to send to support next time?

maria_support: We recommend logging `response.request_id` (python SDK) or `resp.headers['x-request-id']` for curl. Add a small wrapper middleware to your client to emit that to your app logs. Example (python):

```python
resp = client.embeddings.create(...)
print('request_id:', resp.request_id)
```

maria_support: closing loop for now — marking as mitigated. If you hit it again please reopen and attach the rdw-debug bundle + request ids. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: [AUTO] infra alert cleared for infra-7789 — runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/infra-pool-pressure — tag: incident-2026-03-01
